name: Terminus Sui - self-limit synthesis candidate
author: David Lowe
OpenAI Codex
preservationNote: Recovered from the retired draft branch agent/add-terminus-sui-definition during branch cleanup. It is preserved as a non-canonical candidate because the active canonical definition at _definitions/atoms/terminus-sui.jsonld uses the Aristotelian final-end sense.
statementTechnical: Terminus Sui names the recurrent architecture in which sufficiently rich systems encounter domain-specific limits on what they can prove, define, decide, maintain, or irreversibly erase using only operations and resources available within the relevant closure.
statementPlain: At some point, every sufficiently rich system reaches something it cannot fully prove, define, predict, maintain, or erase from inside its own closure.
scopeBoundary: This atom defines the cross-domain recurrence of domain-specific internal limits. Theological conclusions, ultimate-grounding arguments, and applications belong in separate bridge or application atoms with their added premises disclosed.
mathematicalForm: Established domain-specific limits => Terminus Sui as a cross-domain synthesis

theoremDefinitions.name: Gödel incompleteness
theoremDefinitions.definition: A consistent formal system capable of sufficient elementary arithmetic is incomplete; under the second theorem's conditions, it cannot prove its own consistency.

theoremDefinitions.name: Tarski undefinability
theoremDefinitions.definition: A sufficiently expressive consistent formal theory cannot contain an unrestricted truth predicate satisfying the full T-schema for its own language.

theoremDefinitions.name: Turing undecidability
theoremDefinitions.definition: No Turing machine decides the halting problem for every arbitrary Turing machine and input.

theoremDefinitions.name: Second Law of Thermodynamics
theoremDefinitions.definition: For the relevant isolated or thermally closed systems and stated thermodynamic conditions, spontaneous evolution does not proceed toward lower total entropy.

theoremDefinitions.name: Landauer principle
theoremDefinitions.definition: Logically irreversible bit reset has a minimum thermodynamic work/heat cost under the principle's physical assumptions.

citationPolicy.rule: Any public rendering, quotation, or reuse of this claim must include at least one authoritative source link and must preserve the scope boundary. When space permits, render the exact quotation with its source.

citations.sourceName: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems
citations.exactQuote: Any consistent formal system F within which a certain amount of elementary arithmetic can be carried out is incomplete.

citations.sourceName: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — A Philosophical Argument About the Content of Mathematics
citations.exactQuote: Consistency will never be intrinsic to the system; it must always be imported “from the outside,” so to speak.
citations.supports: Metatheoretic outside-language interpretation; not a proof of a divine source

citations.sourceName: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Self-Reference and Paradox
citations.exactQuote: Any theory extending first-order arithmetic and containing schema T is inconsistent.

citations.sourceName: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Self-Reference and Paradox
citations.exactQuote: There exists no Turing machine deciding the halting problem.

citations.sourceName: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Thermodynamic Asymmetry in Time
citations.exactQuote: In the spontaneous evolution of a thermally closed system the entropy can never decrease.

falsificationCondition: A cited theorem is shown not to establish the domain-specific limit attributed to it.
The cross-domain commonality cannot be stated without erasing the source theorems' native hypotheses.
Terminus Sui is presented as an individual source theorem rather than a named synthesis.
